title: Pose two friction-jointed helping hands to cross wire ends over a mark
instruction: Move the two helping-hands arms until the red wire end and the blue wire end cross over the yellow cross on the table, then let go of both arms and leave them there.
context: Solderers (51-4121) pose a helping-hands stand so two wire ends touch where the joint will be made. Its joints are friction-held: they stay put under a light push and move once pushed past their hold, and moving the clip drags the joints behind it. Pushing or poking the clip moves the wrong joints, and pulling the wire itself comes out of its clip. The arm has to be moved by the clip's body and left alone.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are centres in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. Two helping-hands stands, mirror images across y = 0, each a fixed black base 8 x 8 cm (3.0 cm high on the right, 3.8 cm on the left) at (0.42, -0.27) and (0.42, 0.27), and an arm of three gunmetal steel bars 14 mm wide, 24 mm tall, 40 g each, on three vertical hinges with friction: bar 1 from the base 11 cm to a chrome knob, bar 2 11 cm to a second knob, bar 3 (12 cm, with a black alligator clip on its end) from there. Each hinge holds until 0.10 N m is applied, then turns against 0.10 N m with no spring, within 150 degrees of straight. The bars' centres are 4.5 cm above the table (right) and 5.3 cm (left). The clip holds a 5 mm wire stub 5 cm long (3 g, red on the right stand, blue on the left, bare copper tip) straight out of its end face, bonded so that 2 N pulls it out. The left stand is 8 mm higher so the wires pass over each other. Start: the arms are folded, bar 1 pointing 60 degrees from forward (toward the table's middle), bar 2 turned 125 degrees from it, bar 3 turned 40 degrees back: the clips' hinges at (0.365, -0.184) and (0.365, 0.184) and the wire ends at (0.226, -0.087) and (0.226, 0.087), 17 cm apart. A yellow tape cross 3.6 cm across with 7 mm arms lies flat on the table at (0.31, 0).
scoring: Measured from above with a ruler on the two wires' free ends: overlap is how far the ends have passed each other along the wires (negative if short), sideways gap is the larger distance of one end from the other wire's centre line, and mark distance is from the midpoint of the two ends to the cross's centre. 0 if at any point a wire came out of its clip (5 mm or more from its place on the clip), or a part fell off the table. 1.0 if at the end the overlap is 5 mm or more, the sideways gap 2 mm or less, the mark distance 5 mm or less, every bar and wire is still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s), no gripper finger is within 3 cm of a bar or wire, and all of this has held for 3 s. 0.5 if the ends are at most 10 mm short of each other, the gap 10 mm or less and the mark distance 10 mm or less (still, let go or held or not). 0.25 if each end is within 3 cm of the cross. 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: Fold both arms back to the start (each bar's angle as in the setup, clip hinges and wire ends at the listed places) and push each wire fully into its clip. Hinges keep any position, so a rerun needs the arms put back.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Bars, bases and wires collide as boxes. Each hinge is a vertical PhysX revolute joint with dry friction made of a velocity drive aimed at 0 whose force is capped at 0.10 N m. Real helping hands use ball joints: here the arm moves only in the horizontal plane. The wire is a rigid 5 mm box on a fixed joint that breaks at 2 N. Fingers' distance is read from their collision meshes. Meshes are drawn on the boxes.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both hands hover by the clips and close on air, neither stand's arm is moved), demo: 1.0 (success at step 340)
